title: Coefficients you can defend

blocks.text: A gas utility's planning model takes one value per project and start year, and its reviewers check every coefficient by hand. Write two functions in `values.py`:

items: `yearly_pof(age, beta, eta)`: the probability that a main still in service at `age` fails within the next year, for a Weibull failure curve with survival function $`R(a) = e^{-(a/\eta)^\beta}`$.

`start_year_npv(flows, start, base_year, escalation, rate, valuation_year)`: the NPV of a project started in year `start`. `flows[k]` is the amount of the project's $`k`$-th year (costs negative), quoted in `base_year` prices; it is paid in calendar year `start + k`, escalates at `escalation` a year from the base year, and is discounted at `rate` to `valuation_year`. Count every flow.

blocks.text: Write each formula with its exponents named before you code it: which year does each power count from? About eight lines.

      round(start_year_npv(flows, 2033, 2030, 0.03, 0.06, 2031), 3))

cases.says: a new asset's PoF is its chance of failing in its first year
each year of a project's cash flow is discounted by its own number of years
an old asset's PoF is conditional on it working today
with a flat hazard the PoF is the same at every age
a later start escalates from the price base year, not from its own start
every start year is discounted to the same valuation date
